name: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models
problem: Transformer autoregressive generation yields one token per request per forward pass, so a serving engine that schedules at request granularity cannot fill the GPU with work from a sequence that finishes early, and head-of-line blocking wastes most of the batch.
mechanism: Iteration-level scheduling (later universally called continuous batching): the scheduler admits new requests into the RUNNING batch as soon as any individual sequence finishes, rather than waiting for the whole batch to drain. Paired with selective batching, which forms sub-batches only from requests whose operators actually need to run this iteration. Both are now default in every major engine.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: up to 36.9x higher throughput than NVIDIA FasterTransformer at the same latency level, and up to 11.2x better latency than FasterTransformer and vLLM at the same throughput, measured on GPT-3 175B (settings per the paper; baseline is FasterTransformer).
